title: The Dragon Within and the Hardened Heart
english: Who is capable of accusing the mask he has donned? Who has the power to reveal and expose the dragon that dwells within? After a short while, the memory fled to the holy scriptures—to this divine book of Job. Within it, as if through a bodily transfiguration, the shameless and multifaceted complexities hidden in the mind are liberated from the outer facade, exposing the writings of the devil and the demons who are the rulers of all evil and wickedness. For he asks: 'Who will reveal the face of his clothing?'

Because this external variety is merely a surface, supported by a depth of unseen evil, he addresses the calm ones with this: Who can reveal the face of his clothing? That is, who is able to penetrate the thoughts of his heart, since they remain tightly folded up? As it is written, his heart has become like a stone and will not be shaken; it stands like a sharp, unyielding edge [[Job 36:13]]. His heart has turned to stone and cannot be moved; it is entirely hardened and stony, refusing to be driven, refusing to follow the Word, and refusing to yield. He is hard, unyielding, and unrepentant. If a person has drawn power from the devil, they possess this same dragon-like heart—unyielding and uncontrollable. But if someone is like gold, following the Word, they will be refined like a goldsmith's work until they become a golden petal, receiving the true forms of God's writings in Christ Jesus, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen. In Chapter 42, verse 10, the Lord gave Job double everything he had before. In verse 12, the Lord blessed Job's latter days, or perhaps his former ones; his livestock included forty thousand sheep [[Job 42:12]], six thousand camels, and a thousand pairs of oxen. title: Double Blessings After Suffering
english: The text states that affliction required children to be doubled. Observe the livestock: sheep numbered thirty thousand, having begun with seven thousand. Camels totaled six thousand, starting with three thousand. Oxen yokes reached a thousand, initially five hundred. The same pattern applied to donkeys. Sons and daughters born to him totaled ten, matching his previous count. Fourteen children were necessary, along with six, to equal the number of lost offspring. We conclude that sheep and cattle were lost, while sons and daughters died but were not lost. Thus, God granted him an equal number of new children, ensuring double in the resurrection. This made him a father of double the children he once had. If souls perished with death and resurrection were false, fourteen sons and six daughters would have been required. The sacred text preserves the account of him receiving six sons. If he later had fourteen sons and six daughters while discussing resurrection, the children would be tripled rather than doubled, contradicting their original number.

Job lived one hundred seventy years after the affliction, with his total lifespan reaching two hundred forty. How does this align with his entire life span? Precisely: having received double blessings, even the years of former prosperity are counted doubly. He lived one hundred twenty years in prosperity, then one hundred forty in suffering. The period 'after the affliction' refers not to when it ended but when it began. Following four and ten years of illness, the duration of his suffering is noted.

title: Duration of Job's Life and Resurrection
english: He lived for another [numbers] years. For the [numbers] years of the previous prosperity that occurred, the double duration of the later good deeds [numbers] years accumulates. Including also the [numbers] years of the plague, [numbers] years are added, so that after the plague, he lived [numbers] years as recorded. Thus, the double repayment of his prosperity is preserved. Therefore, calculate as follows: he lived in wealth and good upbringing for [numbers] years. In the total decline and the body's affliction, [numbers] years. In the second period of good deeds, [numbers] years, making the total span of his life [numbers] years, as the sacred book states.

Job died aged and full of days. It is written that he will be raised with those whom the Lord raises. Akylas and Symmachus, having come together, read the book, following the Hebrew text. Theodotio concludes the [numbers], nothing missing—neither time nor life. It is also written that he will be raised with those whom the Lord raises, clearly the righteous. For the wicked, he says, will not be raised in judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous. We accept these words, even if not as the entire fabric of the text, but as something woven by the holy ones into the book. Nevertheless, we accept all, having received the book from the fathers.

This is interpreted from the Syriac book. Syriac is now the Hebrew dialect, since Syria is called Judean, and many Palestinians refer to Syriacs as such. Herodotus the historian notes: Indoi, Egyptians, Arabs, and Syriacs in Palestine are circumcised. They call the Jews thus.
